answer: One identity runs one mesa-top ember bed under an 80-credit bond. At the tide-marked start it lights the bed and logs ember temperature at two tide times. An auditor recomputes the cooling curve from the public ember cooling table, burning the bond for a reading over 3 percent off, one curve under two keys, or a reused pair. A rented-ember ring fails: one bed yields one curve, so duplicates show in the log, and a second bed needs its fuel and bond. The kth identity pays 38+5(k-1); the 1000th pays 5033, 1000 fakes pay 2,535,500 plus 80,000 locked, honest agents pay 38 once.
